finding: The odd part of |P| cannot be exactly one of 3,5,11, even when that prime is shared with |Q|. Write p in {3,5,11}, |P|=p*2^a, n=2^K*p^v*R, gcd(p,R)=1. Anchor/divisor arguments give K>=1, v>=2 and both other small primes divide R. Every odd Q-difference divisible by either other small prime must be divisible by p^2: otherwise dilate the appropriate A-difference (first to force p, then the A-difference p to exclude valuation one). Fibres Q_u modulo R have p^(v-1)*2^b elements, from RP+Q. If a fibre had both parities, all its elements would be congruent modulo p^2; restriction of its quotient tiling to p^2-cosets would require |P|/p^2=2^a/p elements in each coset, impossible. Thus every Q_u is single-parity. LL Corollary6.2/T2 applies with shared exempt primes 2,p. Q owns Phi_p or Phi_(p^2), since otherwise P owns both and p^2 divides |P|. Q also owns every prime-power cyclotomic factor from R. T2 and Fourier inversion across R therefore give Q_u(zeta)=0 at a primitive pth or p^2th root, so no Q_u is constant modulo p^2. Any opposite-parity fibre indices agreeing modulo either of the other two small primes would force both fibres constant modulo p^2, impossible. But the unrestricted agreement graph on Z_R is connected, since those two primes are coprime, whereas Q contains 0 and1. Contradiction. This needs a fully written packet and explicit source fidelity review before any adoption.
